title: CTCL Literature Tracker
description: Latest peer-reviewed papers and preprints on cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, auto-collected and summarized.
query_human: cutaneous T-cell lymphoma · mycosis fungoides · Sézary syndrome (CTCL)

bullets: New lab stains (like TRBC1) and advanced imaging (ex‑vivo confocal microscopy) can spot early‑stage CTCL that standard DNA tests miss, helping doctors diagnose sooner and avoid mistaking it for eczema or infection.

Combination approaches—using skin‑directed therapies (phototherapy, topical chlormethine) together with systemic agents (retinoids, interferon‑α, stem‑cell transplant) and tailoring to where the disease lives (skin, blood, nodes)—are now the preferred way to treat advanced disease.

Molecular maps from single‑cell studies reveal distinct CTCL subtypes and pathways (e.g., GATA‑3, CD30, CCR4) that explain why some tumors become aggressive and point to existing drugs (HDAC, JAK, CDK9 inhibitors) that could be repurposed.

Early spread to lymph nodes or the brain, and loss of immune‑recognition markers (HLA loss) after transplant, signal a higher risk of rapid decline, so new symptoms should be investigated promptly and treatment plans adjusted.
